q: 1. Softer variety of steel may e obtained by ...............
explain: The Bessemer process allows for the rapid oxidation of carbon, making it easier to produce low-carbon (softer) mild steel.

q: 2. Cast steel is manufactured by ...............
explain: Cast steel is produced primarily through the crucible or electric furnace processes to ensure high purity and control over carbon content.

q: 3. For high grade instruments the steel preferred to, is ...............
explain: Cast Steel: High-carbon steel made in crucibles is hard, uniform, and suitable for high-grade, high-hardness tools and instruments.

q: 4. The steel used in R.C.C. work is ...............
explain: Mild steel is used in Reinforced Cement Concrete because its coefficient of thermal expansion is similar to concrete and it has sufficient ductility.

q: 5. Oil well cement is generally used for ...............
explain: This cement is specially formulated to set under high pressure and temperature conditions found in deep oil well boreholes.

q: 6. The fluxing agent in the manufacturing of white cement is ...............
explain: Cryolite is used as a flux in white cement to lower the fusion temperature without adding color-forming oxides like iron.

q: 7. The mass of cement present in a standard cement bag is ...............
explain: A standard bag of cement is universally accepted as 50 kg (equivalent to approximately 35 liters in volume).

q: 8. In the manufacturing of cement the nodules form the rotary kiln are called ...............
explain: The partially fused material that exits the kiln is called clinker. It is then cooled and ground with gypsum to make cement.

q: 9. The glass used for security purpose is ...............
explain: Bullet-proof glass is designed to resist penetration and is specifically classified as security glass.

q: 10. A badly mixed cement concrete results in ...............
explain: Honeycombing refers to voids in concrete caused by a lack of mortar to fill the spaces between coarse aggregates, often due to poor mixing or placement.

q: 11. For a 50 kg cement bag water required, is ...............
explain: For standard hydration and a workable mix, about 0.45 water-cement ratio is common. $0.45 	imes 50	ext{ kg} = 22.5	ext{ litres}$.

q: 12. Minimum required water cement ratio for a workable concrete is ...............
explain: While 0.23 to 0.25 is enough for chemical hydration, at least 0.38 to 0.40 is required to provide workability in practical construction conditions.

q: 13. Inner part of a timber log surrounding the pith is called ...............
explain: Heartwood is the inactive, denser, and more durable inner part of the tree that surrounds the central pith.

q: 14. Seasoning of timber is essential to remove ...............
explain: Seasoning is the process of drying timber to reduce its moisture (sap) content to a level compatible with its intended use.

q: 15. A piece of sawn timber whose cross-sectional dimensions exceed 5 cm... is called a ...............
explain: A baulk is a piece of timber that has been roughly squared and has dimensions larger than 5 cm on each side.

q: 16. The main constituents which imparts hydraulicity to hydraulic lime is ...............
explain: The clay content (silica and alumina) in hydraulic lime reacts with the lime to allow it to set in the absence of air (underwater).

q: 17. Which of the following cement contains maximum percentage of di-calcium silicate?
explain: Low heat cement is designed to reduce the heat of hydration. This is achieved by increasing the proportion of C2S (dicalcium silicate), which hydrates slowly, and reducing C3S and C3A.

q: 18. The lime which contains high percentage of calcium oxide, is generally called ...............
explain: Fat lime (also known as high-calcium or pure lime) contains more than 93% Calcium Oxide. It slakes vigorously and increases in volume significantly.

q: 19. The property by virtue of which lime sets under water, is known as ...............
explain: Hydraulicity is the ability of lime (due to its clay/silica content) to set and harden in damp conditions or even under water where air circulation is absent.

q: 20. The normal curing period for lime mortar, is ...............
explain: While lime sets slower than cement, it requires moisture for the carbonation process; a standard initial curing period of 7 days is typically recommended.

q: 21. Plaster of Paris is obtained by calcining ...............
explain: Plaster of Paris (Hemihydrate Calcium Sulphate) is produced by heating Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) to about 120-160°C.

q: 22. Which of the following is not a soft wood?
explain: Shisham is a broad-leaved deciduous tree and is classified as a hardwood. Deodar and Kail are conifers (softwoods).

q: 23. When the timber is attacked by fungus and reduced to powder, it is called ...............
explain: Dry rot is caused by certain fungi that eat the cellulose of the wood, leaving it a dry, brittle, and powdery mass.

q: 24. Most economical of the methods of sawing wood is ...............
explain: Flat sawing (or plain sawing) involves making parallel cuts through the log. It is the fastest and least wasteful method, though it may produce more warping.

q: 25. A thin sheet of wood sliced from a log of wood is called ...............
explain: Veneers are thin slices of wood, usually less than 3mm thick, which are glued onto core panels to produce plywood or decorative surfaces.

q: 26. The rapid hardening Portland cement is obtained by ...............
options: grinding the clinker to a high degree of fineness
adding calcium sulphate to the mixture
burning the mixture at a lower temperature
explain: Increased fineness allows for a larger surface area for hydration, which accelerates the strength development in the early stages.

q: 27. The fineness of cement is tested by ...............
explain: The Blaine Air-Permeability test is the standard method for measuring the specific surface area (fineness) of cement particles.

q: 28. Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the ...............
explain: Vicat's apparatus with different attachments (plunger, needle, needle with collar) is used to find consistency, initial set, and final set.

q: 29. Le-chatelier method is used to determine ...............
explain: The Le-Chatelier test measures the expansion of cement paste due to 'unsound' free lime, ensuring the concrete won't crack after setting.

q: 30. The expansion of cement should not exceed ............... for any type of Portland cement.
explain: According to IS codes, the expansion of cement measured by the Le-Chatelier apparatus should not exceed 10 mm.

q: 31. The normal consistency of Portland cement is about ...............
explain: Normal consistency (P) is the percentage of water required to produce a paste that allows the Vicat plunger to penetrate 33-35mm; it is usually around 25-30%.

q: 32. The final setting time of ordinary cement should not be more than ...............
explain: While the initial setting time must be at least 30 minutes, the final setting time must not exceed 10 hours (600 minutes).

q: 33. The rate of hydration and hydrolysis of cement depends upon its ...............
explain: Finer particles provide more surface area for chemical reactions with water, thus increasing the rate of hydration.

q: 34. Which of the following steel is used in manufacture of rails?
explain: Manganese steel is extremely tough and has high resistance to wear and abrasion, making it perfect for railway tracks.

q: 35. The trunk of tree left after cutting all the branches is known as ...............
explain: Once a tree is felled and the branches are removed, the remaining main stem is referred to as a log.
Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is an evaporite mineral, formed by the chemical precipitation of calcium sulphate from evaporating seawater.

q: 37. The lime which has high calcium oxide content and which sets only in the presence carbon dioxide is called ............
explain: Fat lime (Rich lime) contains high CaO. It hardens slowly through 'carbonation' by absorbing CO2 from the atmosphere.

q: 38. A dry powder obtained on treating quick lime with just enough water to satisfy its chemical affinity for water is called ............
explain: Hydrated lime is the dry, stable powder produced when quick lime is treated with a controlled amount of water (slaking).

q: 39. The process of adding water to lime to convert it into a hydrated lime is termed as ............
explain: Slaking is the chemical reaction where quick lime (CaO) reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2].

q: 40. For the manufacture of portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are ............
explain: The standard composition of OPC is roughly 60-67% Lime (CaO) and 17-25% Silica (SiO2), with Alumina and Iron Oxide making up the rest.

q: 41. Good quality cement contains higher percentage of ............
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is responsible for the early strength of cement. Higher percentages indicate a high-quality, high-strength cement.

q: 42. Initial setting of cement is caused due to ............
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts fastest with water and is primarily responsible for the initial flash set of the cement.

q: 43. The slump test of concrete is used to measure its ............
explain: The slump test is a field method used to determine the consistency (fluidity/workability) of fresh concrete before it sets.

q: 44. The central part of a tree is called ............
explain: The pith (or medulla) is the innermost central core of the tree, consisting of soft cellular tissue, around which the annual rings are formed.

q: 45. The commonly used cement in cement paints is ............
explain: White cement is used as the base for cement paints because it allows for a wide range of pigment colors to be added without being dulled by gray cement.

q: 46. The solvent used in cement paints is ..........
explain: Cement paints are water-based; water acts as the vehicle and solvent to facilitate the hydration of the cement base.

q: 47. The defect caused due to over-maturity and unventilated storage of the wood during its transit is called ..........
explain: Foxiness is indicated by yellow or red stains in wood caused by poor ventilation or decay due to over-maturity.

q: 48. The defect caused by imperfect seasoning, is called ..........
explain: Honeycombing occurs due to internal stresses during improper drying where the interior of the wood cracks while the surface remains intact.

q: 49. The purpose of seasoning of timber is to ..........
explain: The primary goal of seasoning is to reduce the moisture content (sap) of the timber to a level appropriate for its intended use.

q: 50. A badly mixed cement concrete may lead to .............
explain: Honeycombing in concrete refers to voids, cavities, and coarse, stony surface areas caused by mortar failing to fill the spaces between coarse aggregate.
